exposure: Vulvar lichen sclerosus (VLS) diagnosed in childhood or adolescence
vulvar lichen sclerosus (VLS) diagnosed in childhood or adolescence
cohort: 81 women histologically diagnosed with VLS in childhood or adolescence in the Netherlands between 1991 and 2015
finding: Most adults diagnosed with VLS as juveniles report continued symptoms, with impacts on quality of life and sexuality, highlighting the need for ongoing monitoring and care.
mod_finding: VLS as a juvenile does not preclude a vaginal delivery, although there were more high-grade obstetric anal sphincter injuries with vaginal deliveries than expected.
